knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Gross margin uses gross profit, which is sales less direct job costs, as a share of sales. It is not profit after overheads.
Sales belong on the statement net of GST where the business is registered.
A profit that appears when sales sit below the break-even revenue built from the same inputs signals a conflict. Reconciliation is taught in MP-04.

practicalCriteria: Learner builds a twelve-month profit and loss from supplied figures, and every subtotal matches the assessor's recalculation to the dollar
Gross margin and net profit margin are both stated with the sales base named, and both recalculate correctly
Each line is labelled fact, target or assumption, and tax, superannuation and payroll lines are included only with a source
Learner finds the seeded error in an assessor-supplied statement and records the line, the reason and the fix
passRule: 80% on knowledge checks; practical sign-off separate
evidenceRequired: Completed working document for the lesson, saved with its formulas or calculation notes
Knowledge check result (a quiz result is not a practical competence result)
stopWorkCriteria: Do not present a statement to a lender, investor or tax agent until every subtotal recalculates
Stop and escalate any figure that cannot be traced to a record or an assumption label
Escalate GST, superannuation and payroll treatment questions to a registered tax agent
